artifacts.summary: Stage-by-stage audit of the tableau pipeline into BimodalLib: identifies the one hard missing prerequisite (an L-level uniform substitution as data on DerivationTree, compile-verified constructible and accepted by register_theorem), corrects the quoted yield (only 2 of 17 valid formulas at complexity 4 carry a derivation), establishes that extraction is Base-only, measures per-fragment and per-bound yields plus interestingness tiers, flags two verified gate collisions, and recommends the bound for open decision 3.

user_decision.question: Open decision 3 of records/theorem-library.md: what complexity bound does the pipeline run to per fragment and frame class, and does admission filter by an interestingness measure or keep every non-subsumed theorem?
options: Boolean and ModalBoolean at complexity 5, TemporalBoolean and ModalTemporalBoolean at complexity 4; Base only for the theorem half, all four frame classes for the countermodel half; keep every non-subsumed theorem, no interestingness filter
Complexity 4 uniformly across all four fragments; Base only for the theorem half, all four frame classes for the countermodel half; keep every non-subsumed theorem, no interestingness filter
Complexity 5 uniformly across all four fragments; Base only for the theorem half, all four frame classes for the countermodel half; keep every non-subsumed theorem, no interestingness filter
Any of the above, but with admission additionally filtered by an InterestingnessMetrics tier floor
user_decision.recommended: Boolean and ModalBoolean at complexity 5, TemporalBoolean and ModalTemporalBoolean at complexity 4; Base only for the theorem half, all four frame classes for the countermodel half; keep every non-subsumed theorem, no interestingness filter

compiled_gates_run: register_theorem on a substitution-generalized row: PASS (lake env lean, exit 0, axioms [propext, Quot.sound], profile {box}, arity 1, fragment ModalBoolean)
